title: Fishers of men (Mark 1:14–20)
hookLine: the kingdom is at hand, and fishermen leave their nets

lines: A MAN WALKS ALONG THE SHORE.
cards: A lake in Galilee. Two brothers stand in the shallows, throwing a round net out over the water, hauling it in, throwing it again. Down the shore, two more brothers sit in their father's boat, mending nets.
Ordinary work, done with the hands, the same today as yesterday. Then a man walks along the beach, stops, and calls to them. Before long, all four have left that shore.

teach.b: First, the announcement. John the Baptist has been arrested, and Jesus comes into Galilee with a message you can say in one breath.

In the Douay-Rheims: "The time is accomplished, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent, and believe the gospel." At hand means close enough to touch. Repent, in Greek metanoia, means more than feeling sorry.
It means turning your mind around, facing a new way. Second, the call.

Jesus sees Simon and his brother Andrew casting their nets into the sea, and says: "Come after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men." He uses their own work. You catch fish; now you'll gather people.

teach.h: THEY LEFT THEIR NETS AND FATHER.
teach.b: Third, the leaving, with Mark's favorite word again: "And immediately leaving their nets, they followed him."
A little further on he calls James and John, the sons of Zebedee, and they leave their father in the boat with the hired men and go.
Notice what Mark doesn't say: whether they'd heard Jesus preach before, what they felt, what their father said. John's gospel suggests some of them had met Jesus earlier; Mark just shows the leaving.

teach.h: I WILL MAKE YOU TO BECOME FISHERS OF MEN.
teach.b: Simon is the one Jesus will call Peter, and Catholics see in him the first of the popes. A pope receives a ring called the Ring of the Fisherman, a reminder of a beach and men who dropped their nets.

how: Catholics hear the call of the first disciples at Sunday Mass in Ordinary Time, and the pope wears the Ring of the Fisherman as a sign of succession to Saint Peter.

o: people who gather others, as fishers gather fish
the hired men who worked Zebedee's boat
men who sell fish at the town market

games.q: who did what — tap the pairs.
p: left in the boat with hired men

s: Mark tells us what the fishermen felt when they left
Mark only shows the leaving. he's silent about their feelings.
repent, in Greek, means turning your mind around
metanoia: facing a new way, not only feeling sorry.
the pope wears a ring named for Peter's old job

games.q: you're Simon, standing in the lake with your net. a man on the shore says: come after me, and I will make you fishers of men. what do you do?
o: leave the nets immediately and follow.
ask for time to talk to your family.
games.why: "And immediately leaving their nets, they followed him." Mark doesn't say whether they'd met him before.

practice: Jesus called the fishermen through the work they already knew, so name the ordinary work your hands will do today: a keyboard, a steering wheel, a sink of dishes, a child's shoelaces.
Then let your hands rest, still, for these two minutes. If you pray, offer that ordinary work to God, nets and all; if you don't, just notice what your hands do all day, and let them rest.

wordCard.voice: Halieis anthropon. Greek for fishers of people, Jesus's call to Simon and Andrew: leave catching fish, and gather people instead. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: fishers of people, from Mark 1:17.

carryVoice: Your line: they left their nets. Four fishermen, and a shore behind them. See you tomorrow.
